title: Verify keyboard, screen-reader, and zoom journeys
description: Cover all named primary flows with keyboard-driven Playwright tests and document manual screen-reader plus 200% zoom/reflow checks for the release browser set without implying physical print validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard Playwright journeys cover project creation, geometry, content ordering/positioning, safe-area refusal/override, setup attestation, calibration draft, PDF preparation, backup import/export, and recovery
Tests assert visible focus, semantic alternatives, associated errors, announcements, and focus restoration at critical transitions
A manual checklist records browser, operating system, assistive-technology version, result, issue, and tester/date fields
At 200% zoom/reflow primary actions avoid two-dimensional page scrolling except inherently spatial previews
Release evidence explicitly excludes physical printing validation

steps.details: Map each PRD 27 named workflow to keyboard actions, expected semantics, focus checkpoints, statuses, and reusable fixtures.
Use only public UI and keyboard input to exercise the matrix, including non-drag alternatives and refusal/confirmation paths.
Create a release checklist for supported screen-reader/browser combinations, keyboard exploration, 200% zoom, reflow, forced colors, and reduced motion.
Record tested software combinations and outcomes while explicitly separating untested combinations and unavailable physical evidence.
Run keyboard journeys, automated accessibility filters, type, lint, and build checks relevant to the accessibility slice.

technicalNotes: Maximum execution scope is ten minutes; use small fixtures and focused journey filters, with manual execution documented separately.
Manual assistive-technology results are release software evidence, not evidence of physical print placement.
